title: Lord, May Thy Holy Spirit Calm
description: Lord, May Thy Holy Spirit Calm in Tonic Solfa to WINCHESTER NEW, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911).
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre (8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to WINCHESTER NEW; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Lord, may Thy Ho-ly Spir-it calm Our trou-bled souls, and give them rest; And with His touch, like heal-ing balm, Al-lay the pain of the dis-tressed.

lines: Lord, may Thy Holy Spirit calm
Our troubled souls, and give them rest;
And with His touch, like healing balm,
Allay the pain of the distressed.
We hear the promise Thou did'st make
And peace and hope our souls o'ertake,
And joy dispels our brooding woe.
Now let us feel the Spirit's power,
And let us hear His gracious word;
Fulfil to us this holy hour
The promise of our dying Lord.
Come, Holy Ghost, with warmth of love,
With light of hope, and calm of peace,
And raise our sense bound souls above
The mocking joys of earth that cease.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to WINCHESTER NEW by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
